title: Find Your Zone
body:
I have been using the Fabulous app for about two years now. I just started using the Clarity app again more recently. The first time I started using it I wasn’t ready for it, but after using the Fabulous app and working through my schedule structuring of time I have found the Clarity app to be much more useful, particularly as I am back and graduate school for the first time since 2010 when I received my doctoral degree. I am now working on licensing and it is much different than doctoral-level research. It requires turning things in that are good enough, and letting go of perfectionism. The clarity app is perfect for this task. I list out everything that I have to do, then use the AI Centering and Planning to help personalize and prioritize my approach. It’s about “progress not perfection;” a lifelong commitment that I am continually learning to adapt to and incorporating into my professional and personal development. 

If you are serious about real change in how you tackle your every day and work tasks, this is certainly the app for you!

title: Disorganized AI generated content plus an unremarkable to-do list feature
body:
I mean try it out for yourself but I found this to be the opposite of helpful. I cannot  imagine even someone without ADHD finding this app helpful. 

Somehow more pop ups and distractions than their other app ‘fabulous’

ALSO:

1. Before you can even sign up they try to sell you on (I’m not joking) TWELVE (12) other separate apps. 
I get needing to make your cash but it was just annoying. I felt bombarded and almost didn’t finish signing up simply because of this.

2. HAS ONE FEATURE AND ITS UNREMARKABLE: I really wanted this to be the answer to my serious struggle with ADHD but The only feature it really offers is a daily to-do list tracker but it is hard to navigate because there is no “overview” type feature that gives you an ability to plan ahead or move things around or break things down. 

There are only downsides to use this app vs just writing a to-do list on a piece of paper. 

3. EVERYTHING IS AI GENERATED, NOT SOOTHING AT ALL: In addition to the to-do list it also has “advice” but it’s all AI generated videos based on quotes from doctors and others. You can find these elsewhere with much better deliver systems. (I cannot stand the sound of AI voices or the look of the videos—my brain is perturbed by this kind of fake)

4. SUBSCRIPTION SYSTEM (PREDATORY): There’s a ton of reviews about how hard it is to cancel your subscription and it’s true. It didn’t take me that long because I did it on my computer.  I saw all the sneaky roadblocks along the way—I just luckily stumbled into to navigating through them. It’d be hard to believe it’s not intentionally predatory.  Which is not a word I want associated with a program I’m seeking help from.

title: Clean Up on Aisle 5
body:
OK, so first I got the ad, a Google ad at the top of the search results for “alarms and reminders on Mac”. That led to a questionnaire which was fine. Then at the end I had options of $1.00, $11.00, and $16. It was for two weeks and then after that there was a $39 every other month offer. 

Then another screen came up for buy now and I said “Well, is this for the $39 or for the $16?” So I went back but once I went back apparently I lost everything because when I did I was not taken to the previous page, but to the start of the survey. When I hit continue there was the same first question but it was already filled in with the answer I gave the first time. But there’s no button to go on to the next page. I’m just out. I have no navigation at all. 

OK so I go to the App Store and download it. 


**What is the difference between Clarity and Fabulous? Whatever it is, it’s not obvious to me from the AppStore descriptions.**


I am offered a one week free trial instead of the two week free trial I had on the page from the Google ad. I am also offered different payment plans. It has a different questionnaire. And it doesn’t know who I am, confirming that all that prior work had been lost.

I find ALL of that confusing. Tell us that we can’t go back. It would be better if you fixed it so that we could go back and not lose everything but maybe the higher ups don’t want to pay for that. If you’re not gonna do that at least warn people about going back. 

I mean, seriously, do you know what’s going on here? You’ve got your experts who are providing content to people who are actively using the site and then you’ve got your business and marketing people who are working on a funnel and don’t really know all that much about their customers/patients. They put us in this funnel and it ain’t working for us. 

This is the kind of thing the lady who complained about the subscription plan is talking about. The left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing. The left-hand is trying to help customers and the right-hand is just running a business. You need to adjust your business to the target market you are actually working with.

And then, as far as an answer, you directed her to the Help but you didn’t really say “yeah we’re gonna fix this cause you’re right that’s a problem”. So I’m cosigning her problem and adding mine and saying FIX THIS.

The second survey concluded my strengths were hyper focus and creativity whereas the first one said it was hyper focus and adaptability. 


**Why do you have (at least) two different surveys in the first place!?**


What is that about? Are you saying that people who come in from a Google ad are somehow a different market segment from people who download the app? Have you actually done a study justifying that? 

I really think the survey I had at first was actually much better, asked better questions.  I hate multiple choice questions where you get four options and NONE of them are right and there’s no ‘other’ and you can’t write in your answer. You are guilty of that, too, especially on the second survey I got from the app.

This thing is playing music while I’m going through the app. That’s fine, but I need to do something else right now. I opened up a different app but the music on your app is still going. Usually the audio cuts off in my other apps. I go back but there’s no place to turn off the music. There’s an arrow like a play button for a video but again there’s no stop and no sound icon. if I press play can I stop it? Will I be able to turn off the sound? I don’t know. It doesn’t say so. I leave it alone. I have to just close up the whole app.

Yeah, I think there’s some things you need to clean up here. And share this with the staffers referenced herein. Don’t leave it in a pile of survey results in the marketing department that never get studied, used, or responded to. A canned answer about going to the help section is most definitely NOT a ‘response’.

body: This is a predatory app. It advertises to people who have a disorder that makes it difficult for them to remember to cancel a free trial, so they end up paying for a premium prescription they do not want and do not use for several months. I did not find this app to be any more helpful than other free or low cost organizing/productivity/timer apps for ADHD - they are all the same. This app is visually overstimulating with juvenile graphics and a user interface that is not intuitive. This is not supportive to folks who actually have difficulty with focus and attention. And then when you do remember you have this silly, expensive subscription, it is almost impossible to cancel because you have to remember how you signed up (which was likely impulsively), and it took several password recovery attempts through various emails to finally access my account to cancel it. I paid for at least one month extra because of the barriers to cancellation. Anyone with ADHD knows that once there are too many steps, we often give up and say we will get to it later- only for a month to go by before we remember. This was developed by folks who know ADHD well and the vultures have used this knowledge to prey on vulnerable individuals.

title: Incredible App - Gives me hope
body:
I’ve been holding off on writing a review because I wanted to use the app for a bit to review honestly. I was diagnosed with ADHD later in life & knew there were things I had challenges with that I just didn’t know how to overcome. 

From distractions, to time blindness, emotional disregulation, hyper fixation on things that aren’t a priority, etc. It felt like I was in front of a locked door, and I knew I needed a key to open it, but had no clue which key was needed, where to find it, or where to begin looking. 

What’s really beautiful about this app is that it has so many incredible resources to help you on your ADHD journey. It’s not an overload either. It’s educational, practical, inspiring, easy to use, and encouraging. 

There is a community of people you can engage with which I love. Makes me feel understood. & there are journeys you can go on that focus on different daily topics. The topics are tools you can use to manage your ADHD. & it’s broken down into very digestible small bits. 

I’m grateful for this app because I finally feel  like there is a resource that’s available that understands my struggles and is providing me tools to help me manage and work through it. I find that this app is another wonderful tool I can add into my arsenal that caters to ADHD/neurodivergents. 

& to top it all off, there’s beautiful artwork and storytelling! Honestly, you should give the app a try. Doesn’t hurt to see if it can be helpful. I know for me it has been incredibly helpful and I plan on using this app for a while. 

♥️ Big shoutout to the developers & team behind the app!! Appreciate you all, truly.

title: CRASH, CRASH, CRASH
body:
This app  an be guaranteed reliable in repeatedly, non-stop crashing.

Crashes are non-stop, especially when you open a list that you made and attempt to edit the duration. 100% guaranteed to crash. 

My resolution is to always close the app after editing the “to do” item time.  This will crash. Additionally, items that users added (prior to the crash) typically are deleted. 

For a person with ADD, this can be extremely damaging, as you may forget what you previously entered. Don’t rely on the app to save anything. Pen and paper are a better, more reliable fix!

It is also highly irritating that users cannot set a default for duration of tasks (everything is set to 30 minute increments). Users should be able to set this when they enter a task. 20 tasks? Now you have 20 edits and at least 20-40 crashes.

None of users “incompleted”tasks forward to future days. 

So, if you have ADHD and are potentially forgetful (we all are!) due to the bombardment of stimuli… No worries, you will NEVER be prompted to finish a task or to see a reminder “to do” that you enter.

Clunky and inefficient without any double-check.

No calendar options for planning tasks ahead of schedule (procrastinators will LOVE this lack of planning).

Tired of boring, mindane tasks? no worries… This app makes you enter the same information every single day. Do you need routine timers for staying on task, not losing your focus? Well, then this app is not for you. 

I spent about 20 minutes every morning (for 4-6 months) entering my to do list, editing the time needed per event and watching insane amounts of crashes. 

NOT A CALENDAR!
Tasks cannot be repeated. There is no calendar option. There is only today. 

Apparently there’s no need to plan forward or maybe look at the past week’s events, to repeat tasks or time routine tasks that are important (it’s not like people with ADHD get distracted throughout the day and throughout the mundane process of managing their priorities and time).😂

I find myself mindlessly re-entering the exact same information, day-after-day, (tell me why this is better than a manual daytimer???)

The app is supposed to help you get things done and be more efficient. 

I find it to be a time sink. 

TORTUROUS SOUNDS
There is an automated incredibly RANDOM background noise that changes from one task to the other. 8-22 tasks? Expect 8-22 Random, bozarre sounda from your phone. TALK ABOUT DISTRACTING!

Users have no option to select the background noise, many of the “quiet noise“ is beyond irritating. One is like fingernails on chalkboard, a scratching noise, the other is a noisy coffee shop, another one is a noisy public environment (street with cars, talking, horns? 

None of the background noises are custom to the user. Maybe ask user if they have a preference?

Due to irritating sounds applied to my tasks (by the app)I routinely turn-off all sound for the app. 

This basically makes the app useless, because there is no alert or pinging to let you know when the time is up.

While the creators of this app had a good idea, they obviously don’t have a DHD… Or they have no idea how to manage it. 

This app should be a calendar to take it to the next level. 

I am disappointed that I paid for this app. I already have a timer app that isn’t quite as I can friendly… But it is a calendar and it does allow me to repeat tasks and I do receive alerts for upcoming tasks. it’s called “Focus Keeper“ Another great app is Intelligent Change’s “Journal 5” app.

If someone could combine all three of these, THAT would make a great ADHD app!!!

title: Clarify ADHD: A Game-Changer for Focus and Productivity
body:
As someone navigating the challenges of ADHD, finding tools that truly cater to my needs has always been a struggle—until I discovered Clarify ADHD. This app is nothing short of a revelation, offering a comprehensive suite of features designed to empower individuals like myself with ADHD to thrive in their daily lives.

From the moment you sign up, Clarify takes the time to understand your unique challenges and strengths through an in-depth onboarding process. This ensures that the strategies and recommendations it provides are tailored specifically to you, making the experience feel personal and impactful.

The app's focus timer is a standout feature, allowing you to work on tasks without distractions. With customizable music options and periodic reminders, it creates an immersive environment that keeps you engaged and productive.

One of the most valuable aspects of Clarify is its in-app community. Connecting with others who share similar experiences provides a sense of belonging and offers practical tips and encouragement.

Clarify doesn't just focus on productivity; it also emphasizes self-discovery and personal growth. Through guided routines like centering activities and deep work sessions, it helps you build a foundation for long-term success.

While the app is packed with features, it does come with a subscription cost that might be a consideration for some users. However, the value it provides far outweighs the price, especially for those committed to making meaningful changes in their lives.

Clarify is more than just an app—it's a lifeline for anyone looking to harness their unique abilities and overcome the challenges of ADHD. Whether you're struggling with focus, organization, or procrastination, this app equips you with the tools and support you need to succeed. Highly recommended!

title: Don’t pay $$ for apps that purport to help neurodiverse folks but instead take advantage
body:
I am posting this review/warning under both the Fabulous AND Clarify app pages because it is the developer’s dishonest method of not appropriately handling these charges of getting BOTH apps that created this issue.

I want to warn everyone against subscribing to any product offered by Fabulous, an app that purports to help people with ADHD but seems to better practice taking advantage of what can be attributed at least in part to symptoms of ADHD and neurodiversity.

I decided in November to take advantage of the free trial offered. As part of the on boarding, I was also offered a free trial of another app designed by Fabulous supposedly even more targeted to ADHD, an app called Clarify.

I found neither app really worked for me that well, or at least, they didn’t draw me in enough to want to use them. That’s fine—every brain is different, and everyone has different things that may/may not work for them.

Before my free trial ended, I logged in to my account to cancel, and yes, my Fabulous account WAS in fact canceled, and I received confirmation. I looked for information about Clarify, but there was nothing separate, nor did I receive any separate notifications from Fabulous OR Clarify stating that a separate trial was ending and I would be charged.

After canceling, I did not go into either app again.

But recently, I noticed a charge on my credit card from the same day I cancelled by trial. The charge was listed on my statement as “FABULOUS APP PARIS” and was for $29.99. The cancellation email only offers instructions on how to reactivate your subscription; it offers no information or warning about any other subscriptions or apps. In fact, while it tells you how to reactivate, it does NOT even have a single hyperlink connected to any support or account pages.

When I went to look for how to get back into the account page (as I had actually purchased the subscription directly from within the app, and it did not go through the App Store or my apple account, even though I had logged in using Apple), I had to find the original activation email which had a link to my account page. When I finally clicked that link today, I suddenly saw the Clarify account and it showed that it was still active.

I immediately cancelled the account and then searched for a way to contact them to request a refund for this amount that I did not believe I should have been charged, and that was connected to an account that I had never used since I believed I had canceled it at the same time as canceling Fabulous.

There is no support email address to contact Fabulous. You simply submit a request through their site. To their credit, they responded to me quickly, but their responses were wholly unsatisfactory, essentially saying, Too bad!

I received a receipt for my initial Clarify subscription, but I have never received any further correspondence nor receipts from them. The only reason I even know about the charge was from my credit card statement, which, again, does not mention “Clarify.” 

There are terms on the receipt email that state, “Please note, if you purchase more than one Fabulous product, other products may be renewing on separate dates and applicable receipts for those products may be sent separately.” However, once I canceled Fabulous, while I received the cancellation confirmation, I never received ANY separate receipt regarding the auto-renewal charge nor did I receive any warning that my trial was ending. I have received nothing from them whatsoever other than their decision not to refund this money.

This is simply horrible customer service. Had I been utilizing the app even a single time after my cancellation of Fabulous or after the renewal date, or had I allowed the auto-renew to happen more than once, I would understand being unwilling to make the consideration. But that is not the case. Their communication is at best lacking, especially charging a credit card without sending an email receipt/notification after. At worst, it is a ploy to grab some extra money for unused services.

I sent three messages back and forth with their support staff before writing this review. After the first refund denial, I wrote that I would post reviews and contest the charge with my credit card company. Instead, their final response to me, written in faux-apologetic language that equates to saying: , We’re so sorry that we can’t offer you this customer consideration because you’re too stupid to have figured out that nuances of our cancellation policies that require separate cancellations for products that you purchased at the exact same time. (That’s not a quotation, but it is what their message essentially says.)

Their final response to me ended with: “This refund request will now be closed, but please do let us know if you need assistance with anything else.”

Either way, this is not a developer that I would ever consider purchasing anything from again., regardless of how interesting a product may look. I would suggest others stay away as well unless you are ready and prepared to skip having a “free trial.” There’s a good chance it won’t turn out to be free.

As stated in other reviews, which I unfortunately read after downloading app for trial, you have to cancel the subscription on their website, rather than as a subscription managed on your phone. I did this 1 week prior to the trial ending by going to the clarify site and it was very simple to do. However, yesterday I noticed a 29.99 charge for Fabulous, which I was shocked to see as I had already canceled this subscription. Upon further investigation it turns out that the clarify ADHD subscription that I had signed up for was also linked to a fabulous subscription, which is apparently the “parent” app for the clarify adhd app. As I had never signed up for or downloaded the fabulous app, I was unaware that I was required to cancel both subscriptions as I was unaware that I even had 2 subscriptions. I am not a stupid person, I am well educated and technically savvy, so this was not a matter of not knowing how to do something, rather it is a matter of the company being purposefully misleading. So, in summary, I believe that the Fabulous brand and associated apps are purposefully misleading and in my opinion dishonest in their practice and I hope that this review can help someone else make a more informed decision regarding the purchase of any subscriptions through this company.

title: A step in the right direction
body:
I’ve been using the app for about a week so far. As an ADHDer that has spent a significant amount of time reading psychological research papers on ADHD, awareness, flow, motivation, etc., I can see where a lot of the content in this app is rooted. Which is great! There’s clearly research backing this app. 
I as someone with that research experience, as well as experience in therapy, am able to recognize this info and tools and know how to mentally apply it and work with it. However, I wonder how well this information really connects and sticks in the mind of someone without that specific experience. 
I think overall this app is a step in the right direction to developing a therapeutic tool that could help a lot of ADHDers manage their lives, but I think it still needs work. In my opinion, overall the app could use some reorganization/redesigning to focus on the user experience, as it seems a bit haphazard and confusing at the moment. I also think it would really be beneficial if the coaching/learning journey was more so integrated into the overall app experience. 
I like the “deep work room” a lot. The music, the subtle “hey, are you on track?” reminders (like when there’s just a little line that circles the task), the ease of adding in the to-dos and working through your list of tasks - I think this is done really well and I find it to be a pretty seamless experience. It really encourages you to just focus on one thing at a time, leaving space for deep focus while also using subtle cues to keep you on track.  
I also think the cost of the subscription is really high, however if this has the potential of being a very effective tool, it might be worth it. 
Overall, I’m looking forward to continuing to use this and see how well it works for me

title: Not adhd friendly subscription system
body:
I can’t review the app itself, though it looks well thought out and helpful, which is why I’m not giving the app 1 star. I signed up for clarify through an instagram ad and agreed to a certain subscription payment plan after a free trial period. I then downloaded the app and used the same email and password to log in. It asked me again to select a subscription plan- this time with entirely different options. Since I hadn’t been charged for the first one, I thought it was giving me these new (better!) options, if I skipped the free trial period. So I did, and was charged for that amount through the Apple App Store. It turns out, I now have 2 subscriptions using the same account, and will be charged twice. I tried contacting their customer service but it’s been over a week and never heard back. I cancelled the first subscription, even though it appeared (falsely) that I might lose access to both subscriptions (and have already been charged for the second). When I next opened the app, it tried to tell me to renew my subscription. Now I’m just waiting on Apple to refund my purchase so I can be rid of this. 

Long story short- the subscription system is not at all adhd friendly. Though if you go in mindful and use the most straightforward route to subscribe maybe it’s worth it. 🤷‍♀️

And side note, there’s a water drop alert sound from either this app or fabulous (because of course I mistakenly signed up for that subscription at the same time in all of the confusion) every morning at like 1:30am. My phone is on do not disturb at that time, and when I reach for my phone it doesn’t show anything specific from either app. But I know it’s one of them because the same noise accompanied a different notification from them. Very annoying. I’m only keeping the apps for now while I try to sort out the subscription mess.

It basically comes down to being a timer with music for focus work, which is 100% ineffective if your “deep work” focus needs are not in one desk-like place where you can use the timer to remind you to stay on task rather than using your phone for something else. When you need support to stay focused when unpacking/organizing your house while managing contract work tasks, kids’ schedule’s and their various medical/therapy appointments, a phone timer is not going to offer anything more than my kitchen timer already does.

The various learning modules are  kind of like an enthusiastic cat poster with a yoga vibe- every single concept I have already heard many times before. If a pep talk is all I needed to improve ADHD symptoms, I think I’d have been good long ago.

I do give it a second star for offering coaching access within the program, though it also requires too many steps for me to effectively use- a day or two to hear anything back regarding the initial request, and then you have to use a different, out-of-app, platform altogether to access the coaching communications.

If we use tools that work WITH our ADHD, instead of against our ADHD, we can be much more successful. I struggle with the shame and guilt of my executive disfunction and difficulty initiating tasks. This app helps me see I am different and I deserve to use different tools to help me do things my way.
 I also suggest the books: ADD-Friendly Ways to Organize Your Life AND the Radical Guide for Women with ADHD. The Radical guide really shook my world and left me without shame and guilt. We deserve life to be a little easier.

The activities come through with animations where the speed can’t be controlled, so I would read the screen and be waiting for awkward beats for the next part of a sentence. 

I disagree with the idea of a paid trial and shouldn’t have signed up to begin with. The app tells you how much it costs them to pay their team during the trial. I get this in concept, but your product should be great enough that the conversion rate to paid subscriptions sustains the operation without asking people to pay in just to try. It’s portrayed as pay what you want, but I didn’t see an option to pay $0. 

Also, you have to unsubscribe online instead of being able to manage it through your settings on your phone like other apps. This seems intentionally difficult and like a way to ensure people forget about the trial and pay for an auto renewal. 

Overall, I was so overwhelmed by the animations and options that I couldn’t get started and instantly found the app demotivating. I also felt ashamed that I impulsively spent money on yet another thing marketed towards ADHD, which is known to cause impulsive spending and seems to be a target for so many companies.

title: So much potential… not much there.
body:
This app and the same company's Fabulous app started off strong with me! The gorgeous images are motivating and pleasurable (important for many creatives with ADHD, as the minimalist or businesslike aesthetic of other apps makes me want to hurl my phone out the window), the gentle coaching, the amazing deep focus room that makes me actually want to go spend some time there all made me actually look forward to spending time organizing my life and my day. This app does a good job of attracting me to open it for certain goals, like the decluttering challenge.

Sadly, once I got in, there wasn't enough there to support me and actually getting those things done. An ADHD app needs to have both the container for the things to do – which this app does well – and some really concrete paths to lead people down to break bigger tasks down into smaller ones and check them off or move through them along the way. but when I get in to the deep focus room or the cleaning challenge…that's it. Just the pretty container and meditations motivating me, no help actually doing the thing. I set my goal...and then it tells me to go and do my goal, so I feel good temporarily (again, great job giving that initial boost of excitement-interest-can-do-feeling to begin!) but soon I'm kind of floundering around trying to organize my thoughts and getting distracted. I don't want to navigate out of this app and into another one to manage my to do list or to break my tasks down into smaller steps. I was hoping I could do all of that within this app.

So an example: the decluttering challenge. It makes me really want to take the challenge and do one thing each day. But that I open it, and the very first thing and asked me to do is… Check off accomplishing the task! And then the second thing is coaching me through how to Declutter by telling me about four steps in the process. OK… Would it make more sense to tell us about the four steps, then have us check off each step intern while moving through the challenge, and then we get to earn checking off that day? It's just backwards. It makes me wonder if there is a serious investment in making this app work, or if somebody started to make something gorgeous, lost interest or funding or developers, and decided to make money off of people who sign up eager for the promise of it without actually delivering on that promise. 

Or the deep focus room: before you go into it, you could set up a larger focus plus sub-tasks that would be the steppingstones along the way to completing the larger focus. Then you could customize the amount of time you want each one to take. The music or the light could intensify as you're getting close to the end of each allotted time. Then when you check off of a subtask, you could offer some change - different area of the image (moving along a step) or a beautiful sound to feel like you're doing a good job moving through the smaller tasks. 

All of that to say: What's unique about this app is the aesthetic and motivation stuff that I haven't seen anywhere else. Meanwhile, there are dozens of apps out there that know how to do what this one doesn't. So if the developers are serious about helping people with ADHD, this is the only app I found so far that has the potential to really help me. But without the actual help breaking down tasks, organizing the day, and then using the motivational power of the app to move through smaller tasks to accomplish a goal, it's not worth even close to the annual subscription fee. I'm afraid I'm not renewing my subscription. (Developers: contact me if you want feedback or beta testing!)

title: So helpful! Definitely recommend!
body:
This app has helped change my life the past two weeks for me (the Fabulous app is also amazing). I actually completed all my major tasks at work this week, and I finished them early!! I’ve been struggling so much with burnout, procrastination, and exhaustion at work for over a year now. This app is helping change that. 

I love how beautiful the app is - it’s part of what makes me want to go back to the app everyday. The Deep Work Room is great. 

I didn’t give the app 5 stars for one main reason. Once you complete your journey, it feels like there’s not as much to do. More journeys would be great! That leads to the other reason I didn’t give it 5 stars. The yearly Premium Subscription is $10 more than the Fabulous yearly subscription even though Clarify has much less content. If there was a discount for subscribing to more than one app, that would be amazing! Right now, I can barely afford one subscription, so when my free trial ends, I will have to switch to a free account with less content. 

Some other suggestions:
- Make the Centering habit more involved in the app. It threw me off when I realized that Centering was just adding tasks to my Deep Work Room. 
- The app seems mostly focused towards people who work from home. I’m not sure how, but it would be cool if there was different options for those who work outside the home, like not losing your streak over the weekend when you don’t go to work.
- Another thought I had was making it so users could separate work tasks from personal tasks. One of my biggest struggles is keeping up with chores at home. 
- Repeating tasks would make a huge difference! I have the same routine I do every morning at work and I have to add it to my Deep Work Room every morning. 
- This is kind of weird, but it would be fun if the backgrounds and the ambient sounds matched when your in Deep Work mode. I downloaded Ambience, so I’ve seen the beautiful art that goes with the ambient sounds played. It makes the experience a little more special when you hear the coffee shop sounds with the coffee picture. 

To finish, I really enjoy this app which is why I have so many suggestions. I’m excited to see how the app develops and grows.

title: Really love this
body:
Growing up, there were so many people in my family with extreme ADD of ADHD that no one even considered that I might have it as well. I was high-producing, so it was assumed that I obviously didn’t have it. *I* could tell as I got older that I had ambition and drive to do *everything* but couldn’t get myself to follow through on basics of my highest priority. Consistency was a massive weak spot. 

I found the Fabulous app (by this same group) around 2 years ago. The visuals, the content, the focus on habits and the journey approach were all very inspiring to me. I completed most every journey and feature in my own inconsistent but inspired way. 

When I saw they had put out one for adult ADHD, I didn’t even think too hard about getting it, because ADHD was something that *other* people in my family had. Not me. 

Then I saw an article about ADHD online, and I chuckled to myself when I saw that my personality “faults” lined up EXACTLY with ADHD “issues.”

But I’ve always been a big believer in turning your “faults” into assets. And I had used my extremely high energy, open/wondering/childlike approach, and ever-changing focus to achieve some pretty cool things already in my life.

I REALLY like the app’s approach of treating ADHD as a super power, brainstorming how it can propel you to your goals/dreams instead of hindering them. 

The Deep Work room REALLY works for me. I had been using a pomodoro app with a clock-ticking sound to remind my brain to stay focused on one single super important task to feel the dopamine of accomplishment, but the ticking drove my husband a little crazy, even though he would pretend it was fine, since he knew it helped me. ;)

But the Deep Work room music/sound effects are GORGEOUS, so he now LOVES it when I put it going. And I don’t always work optimally in 25 min chunks (I.e. pomodoro approach), so the flexibility of the deep work room timing works for me. 

I also love that there is still a journey going on of training my focus and executive functioning and such important subjects, but the main focus always comes back to The Deep Work room where I actually move my LIFE and my SPECIFIC goals forward. 

Since I have downloaded this app, I have moved my business forward in HUGE ways that usually would take a whole team a few months - but I did it by myself in 3 weeks. 

I have also managed to clean up my house, manage my weight/health better, spend quality time with my fam, and keep alcohol out of my body without feeling deprived (a long-time goal of mine). These are all huge for me as well.

In other words, I have high hopes for this app. Very adaptable. Very beautiful. Very inspirational.

- identify a few tasks to do today (oo! A to do list!)
- set a timer to work on a task for an hour (if I could focus on a task for an hour I wouldn’t need the app)
- listen to audio to de-stress 
- watch a video about a habit you must have 
- take a pledge to “shift your thoughts” 

The ad for this showed some kind of decision tree that suggested it was going to walk me through getting stuff done. It doesn’t do that. At all. It’s all self-generated content and seems to be based on the idea that if the app tells you you can do it, then you can.
